title: Russian Strikes Hit Kyiv Energy Grid, Including Substations Tied to Nuclear Plants
dek: Zelenskyy says a combined overnight attack on Kyiv and surrounding regions targeted energy infrastructure, with substations serving the Rivne and Khmelnytskyi nuclear plants struck.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Flag map of Kherson, the Ukrainian city near the southern front where the localized ceasefire applies

keyPoints: Zelenskyy said Russia used 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles in an attack aimed at Kyiv and the surrounding region, with the energy sector as the main target.
Zelenskyy said substations connecting the Rivne and Khmelnytskyi nuclear power plants to Kyiv and central Ukraine were struck.
Zelenskyy said nine people were injured, including one child, and that Kyiv faced difficulties with electricity, water and heat.
On Thursday, Zelenskyy told a summit in Madrid that every power plant in Ukraine had been damaged in one way or another and that Kyiv needs grid equipment quickly.
body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia carried out a combined attack on Kyiv and the surrounding region on November 7, with strikes aimed at the country’s energy network.

## The attack

According to Zelenskyy, Russia used 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles, and all the missiles were aimed at Kyiv and the surrounding region. He said residential buildings and the North Bridge were damaged, a kindergarten was partially destroyed, and nine people were injured, including one child. He said Russia also targeted twelve other regions.

## Nuclear plant substations

Zelenskyy said substations connecting the Rivne and Khmelnytskyi nuclear power plants to Kyiv and central Ukraine were struck, and that substations were also damaged in the Vinnytsia, Zhytomyr, Rivne, Kharkiv and Dnipro regions. These are the president’s own damage claims; Meridian has not independently verified them.

## Repairs and equipment appeals

On Thursday, at a summit of the Ibero-American Community in Madrid, Zelenskyy said “every power plant in Ukraine has been damaged in one way or another by attacks,” and that repair crews were working around the clock. He asked Latin American and Spanish companies for help: “We need equipment that works with our power grid, and we need it fast,” the Guardian reported.

## Diplomacy

The Guardian reported that President Donald Trump predicted a “very big” deal with Russia that could involve more than Ukraine, after an unscheduled meeting with Kirill Dmitriev, a Putin envoy. Trump said he had not met Ukrainian officials who were also at the White House that day. In the same statement on the grid attack, Zelenskyy said Kyiv is counting on increased bilateral support from the United States.

## Wider context from the same week

The Guardian reported that Russia and Ukraine exchanged overnight airstrikes on Thursday, and that one of Russia’s largest oil refineries appeared to have come under attack. The paper said the strikes came as a second day of talks on Ukraine’s postwar reconstruction and security guarantees wrapped up in Brussels.

The Guardian also reported that a Ukrainian attack on a bus killed five people and wounded 13 in Ukraine’s Russian-occupied Luhansk region, according to the Moscow-backed leader there, Leonid Pasechnik. Those figures come from Pasechnik and have not been verified by Meridian.

Zelenskyy’s appeal for grid equipment, as reported by the Guardian, was aimed at Latin American and Spanish businesses. He said Ukraine needs equipment that works with its specific power grid and needs it quickly, while repair crews keep working around the clock on damaged plants and lines.

## How the attack is being described

Zelenskyy framed the November 7 attack as a sign that Moscow is preparing for trilateral negotiations by targeting critical infrastructure, according to UA.NEWS. That reading is the president’s own assessment and is presented here as his view, not as a verified finding.

Kyiv residents were left facing disruptions to electricity, water and heat, Zelenskyy said. He urged partners not to leave Ukraine on its own, and said Kyiv is counting on increased bilateral support from the United States and on unity between both parties in Congress on Ukraine.

## Next steps

Meridian will update this story if Ukrainian or Russian officials release verified damage assessments, restoration timelines or casualty totals for the November 7 attack.

## What we do not know

Meridian has not confirmed the scale of outages, repair timelines, or any Russian response to the attack.
